review.body_prefix: Thanks for making CmdPal event delivery resilient per subscriber. I found three lifecycle edge cases to address so dead RPC recipients and cleanup failures cannot keep extensions active or interrupt later notifications.

actions.note: This action includes two apply-ready inline suggestions plus one separate general PR conversation comment. Do not post without explicit approval and a final freshness check.

proposed_comments.title: Remove disconnected subscribers through the lifetime-aware accessor
proposed_comments.body:
### Remove disconnected subscribers through the lifetime-aware accessor

**Severity:** `high`

This call omits the dead-recipient removal callback, so a disconnected RPC proxy remains in `InternalItemsChanged`. `ReconcileLoadState()` therefore continues treating the page as subscribed, which can keep Performance Monitor background work active and retry the dead proxy on every update. Remove the handler through the public accessor so the existing lifecycle reconciliation can unload the page when the final live recipient disappears.

```suggestion
        EventHelpers.Raise(handlers, this, new ItemsChangedEventArgs(totalItems), handler => ItemsChanged -= handler);
```

Please also update the disconnected-HRESULT test cases to expect the dead callback only once.

confidence.rationale: The changed call passes no cleanup callback while the retained delegate is the page's load-lifetime signal; the corrected path compiled and all focused lifecycle tests passed.

proposed_comments.title: Keep cleanup failures from interrupting event delivery

confidence.rationale: An exception from the callback deterministically escapes the current catch block and stops the invocation loop; the added regression test reproduced the control-flow gap and passed with the fix.

proposed_comments.title: Make Time and Date dead-subscriber removal idempotent and lifetime-aware
proposed_comments.body:
### Make Time and Date dead-subscriber removal idempotent and lifetime-aware

**Severity:** `high`

`OnLoadDynamicListPage` also omits disconnected-recipient cleanup, so stale host proxies remain subscribed and `_loadCount` can keep the page's live updates running indefinitely. Simply routing cleanup through the current `remove` accessor is unsafe because that accessor decrements `_loadCount` even when the handler was already removed; a later host cleanup can therefore unload while another subscriber is still active. Under `_loadLock`, derive the loaded transition from whether the actual invocation list changes between empty and non-empty, snapshot handlers before dispatch, remove disconnected handlers through that idempotent accessor, contain cleanup-transition failures, and update the disconnected-HRESULT regression cases to expect one failed callback. This is a general review note because the safe correction spans unchanged accessor code and the changed dispatch hunk, so it cannot be represented as one honest apply-ready suggestion.

confidence.rationale: The current counter is decremented for unknown or already-removed delegates, while the disconnected proxy remains retained without a callback; focused tests confirmed correct lifetime transitions and one-shot dead-recipient removal after the fix.

proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The safe fix spans the unchanged custom event accessor, its lifetime bookkeeping, the changed dispatch line, and regression expectations; GitHub cannot represent it as one current RIGHT-side suggestion.
